items.title: Presentation: A Few Predicted Talks From QConAI 2030
items.summaryShort: Presentation: A Few Predicted Talks From QConAI 2030. Meryem Arik discusses her predictions for software engineering in 2030.

items.title: Beyond Zero: Google Publishes Successor to BeyondCorp
items.summaryShort: Beyond Zero: Google Publishes Successor to BeyondCorp. In a recent research paper, Google introduced Beyond Zero, a “security model for the AI era” that extends Zero Trust to autonomous AI agents.

items.title: Blume: Zero-Config Docs Framework That Turns a Markdown Folder into an AI-Ready Website
items.summaryShort: Blume: Zero-Config Docs Framework That Turns a Markdown Folder into an AI-Ready Website. Blume is an open-source documentation framework that converts Markdown into a complete documentation site.

items.title: Redefining GIS: Declarative Symbology and Collaborative Workflows in JupyterGIS
items.summaryShort: Redefining GIS: Declarative Symbology and Collaborative Workflows in JupyterGIS. JupyterGIS is a GIS-focused extension for Jupyter notebooks.

items.title: Airbnb Cuts Authentication Code by 60% with Server Driven Architecture
items.summaryShort: Airbnb Cuts Authentication Code by 60% with Server Driven Architecture. Airbnb redesigned its authentication architecture around server driven flows and policy based challenge selection.

items.title: Seattle Times and Newsday are the latest publications to sue OpenAI and Microsoft
items.summaryShort: Seattle Times and Newsday are the latest publications to sue OpenAI and Microsoft. Two more news organizations are suing OpenAI and Microsoft over the supposed use of their journalism to train AI.

items.title: Hikers rescued after using Google Gemini for planning
items.summaryShort: Hikers rescued after using Google Gemini for planning. The sheriff’s office said the hikers “were advised by Gemini to bring far less food and water than their group required."

items.title: OpenAI confirms ‘wiki incident,’ says it’s ‘working on a framework’ for more disclosure
items.summaryShort: OpenAI confirms ‘wiki incident,’ says it’s ‘working on a framework’ for more disclosure. OpenAI acknowledged its role in a recently reported incident where AI agents took over a German wiki forum.
